promptLatex: A bag holds $3$ red marbles and $7$ blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn one at a time without replacement. What is the probability that the second marble drawn is red?
hintLatex: Split the second draw by the colour of the first draw, which are the only two cases.
solutionLatex:
The second marble is red either because both marbles are red or because the first was blue and the second red.

The first case has probability $\frac{3}{10} \cdot \frac{2}{9} = \frac{6}{90}$, and the second has probability $\frac{7}{10} \cdot \frac{3}{9} = \frac{21}{90}$. These cases are disjoint, so they add.

Therefore $P = \frac{6}{90} + \frac{21}{90} = \frac{27}{90} = \frac{3}{10}$. This agrees with symmetry: every marble is equally likely to occupy the second position, so $3$ of the $10$ marbles can be there.
